title: Evidence-bound claim ledger for the 1977 Wow! signal analysis
scope_note: Claims are classified by evidentiary status. Reproducible transformations are not treated as proof of transmitter intent, artificial origin, or extraterrestrial authorship.

evidence.description: Normalized six-sample printer sequence with documented signal-to-noise intervals and midpoint estimates.
Deterministic adjacent-change, peak, reversal, and mirror analysis.
Deterministic zero-baseline Gaussian fit to the midpoint sequence.
Leave-one-out comparison of constant, affine, quadratic, and Gaussian-transit models.
Exhaustive threshold, direction, and polarity comparison against the verified Morse registry.
Exact permutation control preserving the six observed amplitudes.
Normalized printable symbol assignments from ITU-R M.1677-1.
Sourced neutral-hydrogen rest frequency and distinct Wow! frequency estimates.
Jerry R. Ehman's technical account of the observation, timing, and interpretive limits.

claims.statement: The normalized surviving printer sequence used by this repository is 6EQUJ5.
limitations: The printer characters encode receiver-strength bins, not transmitted alphabet symbols.

claims.statement: The six midpoint estimates strictly rise to one interior maximum and then strictly fall.
limitations: The result describes the retained six-sample envelope and does not identify its physical cause.

claims.statement: A zero-baseline Gaussian transit model fits the six midpoint estimates with small residuals.
limitations: Model fit establishes shape compatibility, not source identity.

claims.statement: Under the repository's predeclared leave-one-out comparison, the Gaussian-transit model has the lowest held-out error of the four tested models.
limitations: The ranking applies only to the declared candidate models and six retained samples.

claims.statement: The central two-high/four-low threshold partition maps to the International Morse question mark when high is assigned to dash.
limitations: The threshold and polarity are analyst-declared transformations, not recovered transmitter metadata.

claims.statement: The same central threshold partition maps to the International Morse comma when high is assigned to dot.
limitations: The opposite-polarity match demonstrates that the symbolic interpretation is non-unique.

claims.statement: Under the exact six-value permutation control and both directions and polarities, the question-mark correspondence occurs in 96 of 720 unique orderings.
limitations: This is an exchangeability control over temporal orderings, not a probability that the historical source was artificial.

claims.statement: The repository preserves distinct sourced Wow! frequency estimates and computes each offset from the neutral-hydrogen rest frequency without merging them.
limitations: Frequency proximity alone does not establish artificial origin or intentional selection.

claims.statement: A stable artificial carrier or beacon is compatible with the coarse retained strength envelope.
limitations: Natural emission and other non-beacon explanations remain compatible with the surviving measurements.

claims.statement: PRESENCE, TRANSIT, BEACON, HYDROGEN, and QUESTION may be used as a labeled five-layer summary of the analysis.
limitations: The five terms do not constitute recovered plaintext and must not be presented as words intentionally transmitted by the source.

claims.statement: The source intentionally encoded a linguistic or machine-readable message in the retained six-sample envelope.
limitations: The surviving data do not preserve the timing, phase, or fine spectral structure needed to establish a payload.

claims.statement: The historical event was produced by extraterrestrial technology.
limitations: Compatibility with an artificial carrier is not evidence sufficient to identify extraterrestrial technology.
